final_message:
The bug is fixed, and the full suite now passes (25 tests, including the new one).

The cause was in `records_in_period` in `billing/usage.py`. It filtered usage with `start < timestamp < end`, so a record stamped exactly at the period start was dropped. I changed it to `start <= timestamp < end`. The start of a period is now included and the end stays excluded. The record one millisecond before the start is still left out, as the test expects.

I wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}`.

I also added your reproducing test as a new file, `tests/test_usage_period.py`.

steps.command: sed -i 's/if start < record\["timestamp"\] < end\]/if start <= record["timestamp"] < end]/' billing/usage.py && echo '{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_usage_period.py <<'EOF'


def test_usage_outside_period_not_billed(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.api_calls["id"], 0)])
    start_ms = sub["current_period_start"] * 1000
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 7, timestamp=start_ms - 1)
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 5, timestamp=start_ms)
    created = world.advance_days(31)
    assert created[0]["lines"][0]["quantity"] == 5
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
